Description:
- Critical owner-reported startup failure at https://habitica-companion.pages.dev on iOS in Safari and the installed application. Both supplied screenshots show an unavailable page with the exact error "Response served by service worker has redirections". Investigate and fix the service-worker/navigation response failure so the application opens.

Expected behavior:
- The affected iOS Safari and installed PWA launch successfully without the reported service-worker redirect error. Preserve existing local data and offline-shell/security boundaries; verify Chrome regression behavior. Report physical-device results and any unverified paths explicitly.

Current context:
- Chrome appears to work according to the owner; the Chrome platform/version and iOS/Safari versions are unspecified. The exact failing route, cache/install state and root cause remain unverified. The release worker is src/Habitica.WebApp/wwwroot/service-worker.published.js; existing coverage includes tests/Functions/pwa.test.mjs. The broader mobile release gate T-d76d2a9a-1318-4e63-9bb4-73f620b108cc is related context, not a duplicate of the concrete startup incident or an implicit dependency.

Source:
- Owner request on 2026-10-30 with two iPhone screenshots, retained as skill-tree/history/intake/2026-10-30-ios-service-worker-redirect/photo-1.jpg and skill-tree/history/intake/2026-10-30-ios-service-worker-redirect/photo-2.jpg.

Priority rationale:
- The owner explicitly classified the incident as critical and requested the highest priority. Startup is blocked in both reported iOS entry points. Priority 107 exceeds the inspected queue maximum of 106.
title: Fix critical iOS Safari and installed PWA startup failure from service-worker redirects
